newsitem.title: UK: Russia takes knock in languid emerging debt market.
newsitem.headline: Russia takes knock in languid emerging debt market.

text.p: Russian debt dropped on Tuesday in an otherwise listless emerging debt market which is focusing more on U.S. economic data, traders said.
Overall prices are about in line with the previous day to a touch softer.

Traders said there is little volume at the moment as the market, which has seen a sharp downward correction this month, tracks U.S.Treasuries and now waits for the next set of U.S. data, including the first look at third quarter gdp on Wednesday.
"Everybody has made so much money this year. Now is the time to slow things down, collect our bonuses and look to next year," a European bank trader said.
Though the fall since early October has been severe, traders remain convinced that it has less to do with a change of mood and is essentially profit-taking.
The J.P. Morgan EMBI index, at 274.20, is down four percent from its record high on October 8.
It is still 23.50 percent up so far this year.
However, one of the biggest gainers, Russia, was hit again in early trading, with confidence undermined by fears that another $50 million in face value of MinFin bonds had been frozen.
MinFins fell by up to 1.5 points, spilling over into Vneshekonombank debt.
Dollar Vnesh is now down about 1-1/2 points from Monday morning, with bids at 71-1/2 percent of face value.

One Russian debt trader said the latest concerns over MinFins have only created more confusion over the issue which has plagued the market much of this year after Russian authorities froze a number of stolen MinFin bonds.
Elsewhere, a number of Bradys opened a little weaker but traders doubt there will be much fresh activity this week unless U.S. Treasuries suddenly change direction.
